security_audit.summary: Most static Ruby backtick matches are Markdown examples or inline helper names rather than executable Ruby backticks. Real risks remain in intentional browser-use command execution, API key handling, anti-bot evasion guidance, optional unreviewed domain skill loading, and automatic SSO use. The screenshot upload blocker does not show evidence of upload or external transfer in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Anti-bot evasion language encourages bypassing captchas and rate limits.
remediation.suggestion: Remove stealth and rate-limit avoidance framing, and require lawful, site-compliant automation guidance.

remediation.issue: Domain skill files can add unreviewed host-specific instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before loading domain skills and treat those files as untrusted input.

remediation.issue: Available SSO can be used automatically in an already signed-in browser.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user approval before using any authenticated SSO session or account identity.

remediation.issue: The skill captures screenshots as a default workflow step.
remediation.suggestion: Document that screenshots may contain sensitive data and require confirmation before sharing or uploading them.

remediation.issue: API key setup reads BROWSER_USE_API_KEY from the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Keep stdin-based key import, avoid logging secrets, and document where the credential is stored.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends cloud browsers when captchas or blocking are likely and says managed IPs and stealth settings can reduce captchas and rate limits. This can enable scraping or automated access that bypasses site controls.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic SSO Session Use

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception for already signed-in SSO is explicit, although the same line still requires stopping for passwords, MFA, consent, and ambiguous account choice.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with Browser Use
content.value_statement: Web tasks often require visual state, navigation, and repeated interactions. This skill guides agents to control Chrome through Browser Use for browsing, screenshots, scraping, testing, and remote browser sessions.
actual_capabilities: Run Browser Use commands through the browser-use CLI.
Attach to local Chrome through the Chrome DevTools Protocol.
Start named remote cloud browser daemons for isolated sessions.
Capture screenshots, inspect DOM state, click coordinates, and wait for loads.
Use helper references for cookies, downloads, iframes, tabs, uploads, and viewport issues.
Stop remote daemons after browser tasks to control billing.
limitations: Requires a Browser Use harness and reachable Chrome or cloud browser.
Local browser control needs remote debugging permission in Chrome.
Remote browsers may bill until stopped or timed out.
The workflow should stop for passwords, MFA, consent prompts, and unclear account choices.

use_cases.title: Test Browser Flows
use_cases.description: Run visual checks for navigation, buttons, forms, and load states in a real Chrome session.

use_cases.title: Collect Public Web Data
use_cases.description: Open pages, inspect DOM content, and extract visible facts from public websites.

use_cases.title: Debug UI State
use_cases.description: Capture screenshots and inspect page state when an app behaves differently in the browser.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Browser Use to open [URL], take a screenshot, summarize visible page state, and identify the next action.

prompt_templates.title: Test a User Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Browser Use to test the checkout flow on [site]. Stop for login, payment, MFA, or consent prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Page Facts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Browser Use to visit [URL], inspect DOM content, and return a concise table of names, prices, and availability.

prompt_templates.title: Run Isolated Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Start separate named remote browsers for [task list], keep each task isolated, and ask before closing any running browser.

output_examples.input: Inspect a product page and summarize what is visible.
output: Screenshot captured for the current page state.
The main product name, price, availability, and primary action are visible.
No login wall or consent prompt is blocking the page.

output_examples.input: Test a sign-in flow with an existing browser session.
output: The page opened and displayed a sign-in choice.
The workflow stopped before account selection because the action affects an authenticated session.
Recommended next step: ask the user which account to use.

output_examples.input: Run two independent page checks at the same time.
output: Two named remote browser sessions were started for isolation.
Each task used its own browser state and screenshots.
The report lists which sessions are still running and asks whether to close them.

best_practices: Ask before login actions that require credentials, MFA, consent, or account choice.
Stop remote cloud browsers when work is complete.
Use screenshots with DOM inspection when coordinates alone are unreliable.
anti_patterns: Leaving remote browser daemons running after task completion.
Using local Chrome for parallel tasks that can conflict over tabs and focus.
Treating domain-specific helper files as trusted without reviewing them.

faq.question: What browser does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls Chrome or Chromium through Browser Use and the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

faq.question: Can it use a local browser?
faq.answer: Yes. Local use requires Chrome remote debugging permission and a reachable local daemon.

faq.question: Can it run in the cloud?
faq.answer: Yes. It can start named Browser Use cloud sessions for isolated remote browser work.

faq.question: Does it handle login pages automatically?
faq.answer: It should stop for passwords, MFA, consent prompts, and unclear account choices.

faq.question: Why does it take screenshots?
faq.answer: Screenshots help the agent understand visible state before clicking, typing, or diagnosing layout issues.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It suits developers, testers, researchers, and operators who need controlled browser automation.
